title: Policies
description: Covers company policies related to drugs & alcohol, working hours, sickness reporting, errors/violations, mobile phone use, personal electrical equipment, MFA, and Care First.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are your responsibilities in relation to the drugs and alcohol policy?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Do not drink less than 12hrs before duty. Do not take non-prescribed drugs. Do not attempt to sign on if under influence. Report prescribed drugs ASAP. Report any drink driving conviction immediately. No alcohol/drugs permitted at work.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: You can drink up to 8 hours before duty if it's only beer.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Prescribed drugs do not need to be reported unless they make you drowsy.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: You only need to report a drink driving conviction if it happens while on duty.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: The policy mandates a strict 12-hour alcohol-free period before duty, zero tolerance for non-prescribed drugs, and immediate reporting of prescribed medication and any drink driving convictions. Bringing alcohol or drugs to work is prohibited.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are the limits on working hours?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Max 12 hrs per shift. Max 72 hrs in 7 consecutive days. Minimum 12 hrs rest between shifts (safety critical). Max 13 days work in a row (must have 14th day off).
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Max 10 hrs per shift and max 60 hrs in 7 days.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Max 12 hrs per shift, but no weekly limit if you have 10 hrs rest.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: You can work 14 days in a row if one shift is less than 8 hours.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Working hours are limited for safety: maximum 12 hours per shift, maximum 72 hours within any 7-day period, a minimum 12-hour rest between shifts, and a mandatory day off after 13 consecutive days of work.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What is the personal sickness reporting procedure?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Must inform the depot supervisor at the earliest opportunity if sick and not coming into work. Do not wait until you are about to sign on.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Inform the supervisor within 1 hour of your shift start time.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: You only need to report if you will be sick for more than one day.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Wait until your sign-on time and then report sick if you cannot make it.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Early reporting of sickness is crucial. Inform the depot supervisor as soon as you know you cannot attend work, well before your scheduled sign-on time, to allow for cover arrangements.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are the reasons for having rules and regulations?
knowledgeUnits.definition: To ensure everybody is working to a safe standard and to minimise the risk of accidents, derailments or injuries.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: To make the job more complicated and test drivers' memory.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Primarily to assign blame when incidents occur.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: To ensure trains run exactly to the timetable regardless of other factors.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Rules and regulations exist fundamentally to maintain safety standards across the railway, protecting staff, passengers, and equipment by minimising risks.

knowledgeUnits.definition: A genuine mistake that was not intended to happen (e.g., misread stopping pattern, speeding).
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Deliberately breaking a rule because you disagree with it.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Knowing you made a mistake and trying to cover it up.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Any action that results in a train delay.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: An error is an unintentional mistake made despite intending to follow the rules, such as misjudging speed or misreading instructions.

knowledgeUnits.definition: Where you know you have made a mistake and try to cover it up, or you know the rules and deliberately break them.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: A genuine mistake made under pressure.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Forgetting to perform a required check.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Accidentally exceeding the speed limit by a small margin.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: A violation involves intent: either deliberately breaking a known rule or intentionally concealing a mistake. This is distinct from an unintentional error.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are your responsibilities in relation to the mobile phone policy?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Ensure your phone is switched off in an active cab. Ask anyone entering the cab to ensure theirs is off. If using a mobile for duty (e.g., company issued), ensure you are in a position of safety and not distracted.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: You can use hands-free kits while driving the train.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Personal phones can be used in the cab if on silent mode.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Only video calls are prohibited in the active cab.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Personal mobile phones must be switched off in an active driving cab to avoid distraction. Anyone entering must also switch theirs off. Duty-related mobile use requires being in a safe position and maintaining focus.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are your responsibilities regarding the use of personal electrical equipment?
knowledgeUnits.definition: No personal electrical equipment (radios, MP3 players, headphones, personal iPads/computers, personal mobiles) should be used in the cab while driving. Company iPads for duties (e.g., TAS) can be used once trained, ensuring no distraction.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Personal headphones can be used in one ear only while driving.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Personal iPads are allowed for checking schedules if the train's system fails.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Only equipment that requires mains power is banned; battery devices are okay.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: To prevent distraction, personal electrical equipment is prohibited in the active cab. Only company-issued and approved devices, like iPads for specific work tasks (after training), may be used cautiously.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are the risks of using personal electrical equipment?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Distraction leading to errors, walking into unsafe areas, tripping/falling. Using headphones/earphones prevents hearing warnings or GSMR calls.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: The main risk is draining the train's auxiliary power supply.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: The primary risk is interference with the train's signalling systems.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: The only significant risk is dropping the equipment onto the controls.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Using personal electrical equipment poses significant safety risks through distraction (not focusing on driving or surroundings) and by impairing hearing, which prevents awareness of auditory warnings or critical communications.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are the requirements of the MFA (Managing for Attendance) policy?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Triggered by 5 days total absence or 2 instances in 13 weeks, OR 10 days total or 5 instances in 52 weeks. Stages involve informal/formal chats with managers/union reps, potentially leading to dismissal.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Triggered only after 10 consecutive days of absence.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Involves immediate dismissal after 3 instances of absence in a year.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Applies only to absences not covered by a doctor's note.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: The MFA policy is triggered by specific patterns of absence (frequency or total days). It follows a staged process involving discussions and warnings, aiming to manage attendance issues.

knowledgeUnits.definition: A free phone number offering confidential counselling, information, and advice on personal issues like stress, finances, home life, or bullying.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: A policy outlining first aid procedures in the workplace.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: A customer service charter focused on passenger care.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: A program for reporting safety concerns anonymously.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Care First is an employee assistance program providing confidential support for various personal and work-related issues through a dedicated, free phone line.
